newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech finmin capital markets head resigns.
newsitem.headline: Czech finmin capital markets head resigns.

text.p: Czech Deputy Finance Minister Vladimir Rudlovcak, facing heavy criticism for his management of the country's capital markets oversight authority, submitted his resignation on Thursday, a ministry spokeswoman said.
Ludmila Nutilova said in a statement that Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik had accepted Rudlovcak's resignation.
It said that Kocarnik had named Jiri Spicka, director of the ministry's section on finance and banking, as Rudlovcak's replacement.

"In his resignation it was presented that in the situation when there is a long-term strong media campaign against the Finance Ministry and himself especially, that his continuation in the function of deputy minister would not be profitable for the (ministry)," Nutilova said.
"...especially for the activity of the (capital market) oversight, in which his authority is continually eroded through the systematic attacks."

Rudlovcak and the ministry have been harshly criticised by media and investors for what many have said is the poor regulation of the country's funds and equities markets which are frequently accused of being intransparent and rife with insider trading.
